item.title: 'We are not robots': Mauricio Pochettino's emotional USMNT goodbye was anything but business as usual
item.description: CINCINNATI — Mauricio Pochettino went through Tuesday's U.S. match like every other during his two-year spell. "It was a normal game," he said. "You are focused. You want to concentrate. You want to win. You want to help the players perform." And then the end came — the end of a 2-0 victory over Haiti , the end of a two-leg CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal that completed an 8-0 aggregate wipeout, and the end of a 37-match tenure that saw advances in the program at large but also disappointment in not advancing deeper at the World Cup. When it was over at TQL Stadium, the finality of it all hit Pochettino hard. He's passionate about people and soccer. While his decision to sign with Manchester United was purely business, his emotions about leaving behind a tight group were genuine. "When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things," he said. "Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything." There were hugs and tears, both on the field and in the locker room. "It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us," he said. "When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are not robots." Mauricio Pochettino and members of the team staff pose for a picture on the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Captain Tyler Adams observed, "He fell in love with the country. That's first and foremost, the most important thing. He didn't know exactly what to expect when he took the job. He fell in love with the people. He fell in love with the football, and he fell in love with our team. That's special." Adams and the rest of the team sent Pochettino off in style with six consecutive victories, including four shutouts in a row. "We wanted to finish in a good way," Pochettino said. "The way we play, that is what we dream of when we arrive. The team really enjoyed playing football, playing soccer." In the first half, Christian Pulisic scored on an audacious bicycle kick and teenager Julian Hall continued the torrid start to his international career by scoring for the fifth time in six matches. Weston McKennie set up both goals. "It was a pretty bad cross, to be honest. I had to save him," Pulisic joked about his longtime friend's assist. "I saw it and I had to go for it. It was cool; it was special." Asked if he too had ever scored such a goal, McKennie said, "I've had side volleys, never bikes. I don't know if I'd survive the fall after that." The postgame mood was light, fun and emotional; it was human. item.title: Victor Wembanyama’s ridiculous self-assisted dunk steals the show despite Spurs’ 105-93 loss to Pistons
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama produced another highlight-reel moment against the Detroit Pistons, throwing the ball off the backboard before catching it and finishing with a one-handed dunk. The San Antonio Spurs star used his incredible height and creativity to get past Ausar Thompson early in their meeting with Detroit. Wembanyama had already been blocked by one of the Thompson twins this season, but he found a different way to attack the basket this time. Victor Wembanyama’s self-assisted dunk steals the show against Detroit Pistons The 22-year-old drove towards the paint just over a minute into the game before sensing pressure from Thompson. Rather than force his way through the defence, Wembanyama threw the ball against the backboard, collected it in the air and threw down a one-handed finish. It was a reminder of the unusual skills that make the Frenchman such a difficult player to defend. At 7-foot-4, Wembanyama has the size to dominate near the rim, but his ability to improvise makes him even more dangerous. He entered the contest averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds through 14 appearances, ranking third and fifth in the NBA in those categories respectively. However, the highlight did not tell the full story of the night for San Antonio. Despite Wembanyama finishing with 25 points and 18 rebounds, the Spurs fell to a 105-93 defeat against Detroit at the Frost Bank Center. Dylan Harper added 20 points, while Julian Champagnie scored 14. Detroit also had the final say in the battle of the big moments, with Cade Cunningham producing a poster dunk over Wembanyama near the end of the first quarter. The defeat leaves San Antonio with a 12-3 record after starting the season strongly. item.title: Raptors Lose 15th Straight To Knicks: 4 Takeaways From Eastern Conference Thriller
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Just two nights removed from their overtime loss on Sunday , the Toronto Raptors had a chance to set things right with a rematch against the New York Knicks . This time, to their credit, the Raptors came out firing with a 29-point first quarter that took the champs by surprise. By the end, however, it was the Knicks that overwhelmed, riding the play of their stars to win their second straight game (111-102) and 15th straight against the Raptors in particular. As usual, Jalen Brunson led the way for New York. In 34 minutes, he finished with 31 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 45.5% shooting from the field (4-11 from three). At shooting guard, Mikal Bridges dropped 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field (2-5 from three), while center Karl-Anthony Towns dropped 16 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists, and one steal on 77.8% shooting from the field (1-2 from three). For the Raptors, Ja’Kobe Walter led the way with 25 points, one rebound, two assists, and two steals on 60.0% shooting from the field (7-12 from three). Veteran swingman RJ Barrett , meanwhile, contributed 22 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 52.9% shooting from the field (2-8 from three). Finally, there’s Scottie Barnes : 20 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks on 50.0% shooting (1-2 from three). Whether it was the support of their home crowd or the desperation of not wanting to lose to the same team in back-to-back games, the Raptors came out with a lot of energy in this game, playing with an almost desperate urgency during the early minutes of the game. Eventually, though, that urgency turned to frustration as the Knicks got increasingly comfortable and expanded their lead down the stretch. In the grand scheme of things, this game likely won’t be remembered for long, but it told us a lot about where these teams are headed going into the Holiday season (NBA Christmas and Cup Finals). For the Knicks especially, it’s a step in the right direction that could signal an upcoming shift in the hierarchy. 1. item.title: Greenwich holds off Ridgefield for 4th straight Class LL girls swimming title, 33rd overall
item.description: Greenwich is ready to dive into the pool at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center in West Hartford after capturing the Class LL girls swimming championship on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HARTFORD - The Greenwich and Ridgefield girls swimming and diving programs have engaged in plenty of battles over the years, and the CIAC Class LL championship meet on Tuesday night at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center was no different. For the Cardinals, depth turned out to be key as they captured their fourth straight Class LL title and 33rd overall in program history. Greenwich scored 924 points to second-place Ridgefield's 878.5. Amity was third with 510.5 points. "I felt pretty confident going into this because I knew that everyone on the team has been working super hard, and I had a lot of faith in us," Greenwich junior Olivia DeVries said. With sophomore Alden Charette's first-place finish in Class LL diving, the Cardinals won three individual events and one relay. Seniors Kensie Worden (50 freestyle, 23.59) and Julia Kozma (100 butterfly, 57.70) won gold medals, as did the opening 200 medley relay team of Charette, junior Sara Jee, Kozma and Worden (1:47.96). Greenwich claimed 18 individual medals, including three golds, three silvers and three bronzes. DeVries claimed bronze medals in the 200 freestyle and 500 freestyle. "I'm super proud of the team because we all have worked so hard in practice. The captains have done such a good job to keep us motivated and I'm just very proud of how hard we worked," DeVries said. "Every single swimmer made a difference, every single spot. If you were in the C final, the A final, everyone makes a difference. We are all cheering for each other, and I think that's what makes Greenwich special." "We had some really great swims from all the girls, but especially our senior class," Greenwich coach Megan Kelly said. "I think it really means a lot to them, and to see them swim with such heart was really great." Senior Ellison Charette was second in the 200 IM and 500 freestyle, and she was part of the second-place 200 and 400 freestyle relay teams. "Ellison, she fought hard in both of her races. She had some really good swims. Overall, I was really, really pleased," Kelly said. "They didn't win the (200) free relay, but they went 1:35, which is All-American consideration time. That was pretty impressive." Greenwich's second-place 200 freestyle relay finished in 1:35.79. Ridgefield's first-place relay of sophomore Zsofia Milak, senior Dalia Katra, sophomore Mary Kelly and junior Ellie Griffin swam the race in 1:35.21, which broke Ridgefield's 2022 state record of 1:35.48. Milak had a terrific night for Ridgefield, winning individual gold medals in the 200 freestyle (1:50.20) and 100 freestyle (50.95). She was also part of the first-place 400 freestyle relay (3:32.60), along with Kelly, junior Chloe Archibald and sophomore Charlie Palmer. Kelly won the 500 freestyle in 4:59.44. Norwalk/McMahon

item.title: Waterford heading to boys soccer CIAC final for first time since 1987
item.description: The Waterford boys soccer team and its student section celebrate their 2-0 victory over Daniel Hand in the CIAC Class M semifinals at Valley Regional High School in Deep River on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. The Lancers advance to their first state final since 1987. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) DEEP RIVER - Waterford boys soccer coach Jeff Emerich was grooving when he heard "Jump" by Kris Kross hip-hopping over the Valley Regional PA at halftime of Tuesday night's CIAC Class M semifinal between his No. 1-seeded Lancers and No. 5 Daniel Hand. Emerich knew, too, that if his boys executed a little more criss-cross on the pitch, they'd be jumping Waterford boys soccer into a state final for the first time since 1987, about five years before Chris "Mac Daddy" Kelly and Chris "Daddy Mac" Smith arrived on the scene. Yeah, it all goes back a ways, and it's funny what stands the test of time. This Waterford boys soccer team of 2026 is proving to be one for the ages. With a 2-0 victory over Hand on Tuesday night, in a game that showcased the breadth of their remarkable skill set, the Lancers are one step away from the first-ever boys soccer championship in Waterford history. Brady Wiseman scored off a left-side cross from Brayden Michonski two minutes into the second half and Jaydev Villa, set up by an inexorable upfield rush by Yaman Qarqour, added insurance with 20:35 to play as Waterford improved to 19-1-1 and advances to this weekend's state championship at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford to face No. 2 Weston, which dethroned reigning champ Tolland 1-0 in Tuesday's other Class M semi. "It's been since 1987 since the last time we made it in, so this is our first chance to go up and compete," Emerich said. "We've never won a state title, and it's been 39 years since we've seen a chance, so we are very humbled that we are able to do this, and we continue to work, and that's the thing that makes these boys special." The Lancers got an emotional boost on Monday when they learned goalie Luke Wilson was cleared from a concussion suffered in the ECC tournament semifinals against Bacon Academy. Wilson set the tone Tuesday night by charging out and sliding to break up a Hand scoring chance in the opening minute for the first of his 16 saves. "I didn't even know if I was going to be able to play this game, especially last week, watching when we played Lewis Mills (in the quarterfinals), I was still nervous," Wilson said. "All I wanted to do was get back on the field." Wilson wore a foam helmet for the first time Tuesday night. item.title: Awkward Jim Harbaugh-Justin Herbert Moment Adds Weird Vibe To Chargers Win
item.description: Justin Herbert trade rumros Getty It took nine games, but the Los Angeles Chargers got their first win of the 2026 regular season on Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens. A 1-8 record is not much to celebrate, and an awkward moment in the locker room after the game between head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert just gave the whole thing a very weird vibe. In a video shared on social media which can be viewed here, Harbaugh congratulated the team for the win and then implored everyone to give each other a high five. The camera catches Harbaugh and Herbert exchanging a high five where the signal caller did not look all that enthused as he lightly exchanged a high five with his head coach. Some on social media saw the moment as evidence that Herbert doesn’t like Harbaugh or that he doesn’t have a good attitude. Others defended Herbert, asking whether he should have been doing back flips for their first win of the season. It’s probably just a moment that got blown way out of proportion but when a team has had as terrible a season as the Chargers, every single little moment is going to be scrutinized whether it is fair or not. To give Herbert the benefit of the doubt, it has been a brutal season. He probably doesn’t want to be celebrating too hard when his team is just having a completely embarrassing year. Plus, Herbert has always been fairly mild-mannered and reserved. Mina Kimes wrote a whole profile about Herbert years ago for ESPN which delved into how he is an introvert and just simply isn’t the big personality that many people expect an NFL quarterback to be. Herbert and Harbaugh really do not mix on paper That is what makes the Herbert-Harbaugh pairing so interesting on paper. Harbaugh is loud, bombastic, and prone to outbursts. Herbert is serene, cool, and supremely understated. It wouldn’t seem like the two would work together well but sometimes opposites attract in relationships. The last two seasons the two seemed to work together quite well as the team went 11-6 and made the playoffs each season. Maybe the addition of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is what threw things off a bit but Herbert has remained steadfast in his support of his offensive playcaller . Maybe the moment in the locker room is evidence of Herbert showing his displeasure with his head coach, or maybe it’s just how Herbert is. He and Harbaugh are completely different personality-wise so most likely it is just a case of two very different people sharing a bit of an awkward moment which wouldn’t even be blinked at if the team was 8-1 rather than 1-8. Seeing themselves in last place in the Atlantic Division could do far more harm than good. Unless the team can find some sort of motivation in seeing themselves at the bottom of the division, the only thing the Leafs need to look at is themselves. The club just needs to work hard and focus on controlling the things they can control. Otherwise, the prospect of salvaging this season may be too much to pull off. For now, the talk shouldn’t be about making the playoffs. Yes, that’s a major goal for the organization. But it shouldn’t be the only thing guiding the team’s performance at this point. The guiding factor should be trying to get back to the fundamentals and win hockey games. It might sound like a cliché, but the Maple Leafs have entered a territory in which only the next game matters. While injuries have played a major role in derailing their season, the fact is that the only thing the Leafs can actually do about it is go out there and execute. One can find all the sports adages used to help teams focus on winning. But the bottom line is that the only game that matters is the next one. The Illini just thumped the Blue Devils in almost every way. They outrebounded Duke, 54-34, and Duke had 14 turnovers. Illinois also outscored Duke 31-21 from the line, and ruthlessly controlled the paint. Duke took 40 threes in this game, hitting just 9. Illinois shot just 6-32, but their control of the paint made that irrelevant. And so did the performance of Andrej Stojakovic. When Duke played Cal in 2024, Stojakovic finished with 10 points on 4-14. Tuesday night, he lit Duke up for 46 points on 14-21/2-3 from the floor, along with 16-20 from the free throw line. It was a record-breaking performance: the most points ever scored by an opponent in Cameron was 43 by South Carolina’s Grady Wallace in 1957, when the ACC was 3 years, 9 months, and 15 days old. It came perilously close to breaking Dick Groats’ record of 48 points, set in 1952. He was superb and nearly unguardable, but he’s not the only reason that Illinois won. Quentin Coleman racked up 27, but it was more than that. Here’s something you may not have caught: Zavier Zens, cousin of Kon and Kager Knueppel, who is 6-7, got 8 rebounds. On Tuesday, Cincinnati and Missouri announced a home-and-home non-conference series. Missouri will host the Bearcats at Faurot Field on Sept. 18, 2027, while Cincinnati welcomes the Tigers to Nippert Stadium on Sept. 11, 2032. Although the campuses are separated by fewer than 500 miles, the 2027 matchup will mark the first-ever meeting between the Big 12 and SEC opponents. Cincinnati has now finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2027 season. The Bearcats will host Central Connecticut of the FCS on Aug. 28, remain at home against Missouri State on Sept. 4, and complete their non-conference slate at Missouri on Sept. 18. Cincinnati does not have a game scheduled for the weekend of Sept. 11, when it will either play its Big 12 opener or take a bye. Both Missouri and Cincinnati experienced recent cancelations in their 2027 non-conference slates, making them a perfect match for each other. The Tigers saw their 2027 home contest against Illinois get axed, while Cincinnati’s looming road trip to Boston College was also removed from the schedule. The Bearcats have won five consecutive regular season non-conference matchups, sweeping all three opponents during the 2026 season. The 2027 trip to Missouri will mark the program’s first true road non-conference game since Sept. 14, 2024 when it traveled to crosstown rival Miami (OH). Also, it will be the Bearcats’ first out-of-state non-conference road game since Sept. 9, 2023 at Pittsburgh and first SEC matchup since Sept. 3, 2022 at Arkansas. Cincinnati traditionally had one non-conference vacancy reserved for Miami, as the two competed in one of the longest running series in college football. The rivals played their 129th and final scheduled meeting this past September, making it the fourth-most played FBS matchup behind Minnesota-Wisconsin, Auburn-Georgia, and North Carolina-Virginia. item.description: Nov 17, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino walks off the pitch after the victory over Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match at TQL Stadium. From the moment Mauricio Pochettino was announced as United States men’s national team head coach in September 2024, things felt different. It wasn’t his experience or his personality - although, both were certainly noteworthy. Instead, it was his name. His stature. His reputation. Suddenly, somehow, the United States - the perpetually overlooked, stigmatized name in the halls of global soccer - was dating the prom king. It was unexpected. It was surreal. And it was bound to be fleeting. Now, following a 2-0 victory against Haiti at TQL Stadium, in Cincinnati, the Mauricio Pochettino fairytale is officially over. After just two years in charge of the USMNT (and a whirlwind two years at that), Pochettino departs to take up the coveted / cursed position of Manchester United manager. It’s a change that’s as disappointing as it is unsurprising. Despite the misty-eyed soundbites over the last week in which he described the decision as “one of the toughest” of his career, Pochettino’s return to club football has felt inevitable. He made no bones about his wandering eye, always quick to profess his love for the Premier League while maintaining his London residence throughout his time with the USMNT. Even when his contract extension was announced this summer, the conditions of that deal made it abundantly clear that should an attractive suitor come calling, he would answer. Now, after years apart, he'll get to rekindle that romance. As Pochettino celebrated Christian Pulisic putting the U.S. ahead in the 25th minute with one of the most acrobatic goals of the attacker's career (a high-flying bicycle kick that cut the ball inside the far post), some of his personnel were already across the Atlantic, laying the groundwork for his upcoming rendezvous. Even if his couching staff was divided, Pochettino insisted that his focus was not. And with Julian Hall doubling the USMNT's lead in the 43rd minute, perhaps he wasn't lying. It’s rare that football managers exit on their own terms. Even rarer still when they finish out their tenure having already secured their next job. Likely rarest of all, is to go straight from a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final to the biggest derby in English football. Then again, little about Pochettino's tenure has been normal.
